newsitem.title: JAPAN: Costs press Japan textile firms' ratings - Moody's.
newsitem.headline: Costs press Japan textile firms' ratings - Moody's.

text.p: Japanese textile companies, hobbled by high cost structures compared with their Asian rivals, are unlikely to see their credit ratings boosted in the medium term, Moody's Investors Service said on Friday.

"Japanese textile companies" credit quality is unlikely to show meaningful improvement over the medium term as existing structural barriers hamper improvements in the firms' high cost structure," Moody's said in a report.
Despite their advanced technology and facilities, Japanese textile companies are losing market share to other Asian producers due to the higher cost structure of their domestic plants, Moody's said.
The strength of the yen over the last 10 years has also weakened their competitiveness and import growth has been pressuring their business, Moody's said.
"Improvements are unlikely in the medium term, because of the rigid industry structure, Japan"s unique labour system, and government restrictions prohibiting meaningful improvement," Moody's said.
